acceptedFindings.title: Complete-case analysis without reporting of missing data patterns
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Selective omission of participants with missing data can bias effect estimates if missingness is related to exposure, outcome, or covariates. Without reporting the amount and pattern of missingness, readers cannot assess the risk of selection bias.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide a flow diagram or table describing the number of records excluded due to missing data for each variable, compare characteristics of included vs. excluded participants, and consider sensitivity analyses (e.g., multiple imputation) if missingness exceeds 5%.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: stats-run.json contains only 'completeCaseN':240; no fields for total records, missing counts, or deterministic missingness flags.

acceptedFindings.title: Absence of descriptive statistics (Table 1)
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Baseline characteristics are required to judge comparability across exposure groups, assess confounding, and understand the population to which results may apply. Their omission prevents critical appraisal of the study.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a Table 1 showing distribution of demographic and clinical variables (age, severity, albumin, outcome) overall and stratified by treatment group, with appropriate summary measures and tests of difference.

acceptedFindings.title: Model fit and diagnostics not reported
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without goodness-of-fit (e.g., Hosmer-Lemeshow test, AUC, calibration) and influence diagnostics, one cannot evaluate whether the model adequately describes the data or is driven by outliers. The manuscript only states that diagnostics were reviewed without presenting results.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report model discrimination (AUC) and calibration (calibration plot, Hosmer-Lemeshow test), and discuss any influential observations (Cook's distance, DFBETAs). If no separation was found, state this explicitly.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: diagnostics.json and stats-run.json include aic, bic, max leverage, max Cook's distance, but no goodness-of-fit test or discrimination metrics.

acceptedFindings.title: Lack of justification for covariate selection and confounding control
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The association of interest is between treatment and outcome after adjustment; however, the choice of covariates (age, severity, albumin) is not motivated, and there is no discussion of likely confounders, unmeasured confounding, or a causal diagram (DAG). This undermines the validity of the adjusted estimate.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide a rationale for each covariate (e.g., based on prior knowledge or directed acyclic graph), explicitly state what confounders were controlled, and discuss the potential impact of unmeasured confounding in the limitations.

acceptedFindings.title: Vague and uninformative claims in abstract and conclusion
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The abstract and conclusion merely state that 'interpretable local evidence' was produced and that 'methods review is required,' without presenting the primary result or its interpretation. This does not fulfill the purpose of a scientific manuscript.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Rewrite the abstract and conclusion to clearly state the adjusted association between treatment and the outcome (e.g., OR=1.61, 95% CI 0.84–3.10, p=0.15) and interpret it within the limitations of an observational dataset, avoiding overselling or vacuous statements.

acceptedFindings.title: Data source, ethics, and code availability not disclosed
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The manuscript describes the data as a 'local research dataset' without any details on provenance, ethical approval, or informed consent. Reproducibility requires access to data and analysis code; neither is described.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a data availability statement indicating how others can obtain the anonymized data and analysis code (or, if restricted, the procedures to request access). Also include ethics committee approval or a justification for exemption.

acceptedFindings.title: Explicit separation diagnostics are missing
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: Limitations section: 'Logistic-type model detected; explicit separation diagnostic evidence was not found.'
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Separation can bias coefficient estimates and inflate standard errors, undermining the validity of p-values and confidence intervals. The very wide CI for the intercept (OR: 0.0005–0.667) raises suspicion.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Perform separation checks (e.g., inspection of coefficient tables for extreme estimates, Firth's penalized likelihood, or profile likelihood CIs) and report the results. If separation is present, apply appropriate corrections.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Check if a separation diagnostic (e.g., Firth full model log-likelihood vs. standard) is present in stats-run/diagnostics.json or any companion artifact.

acceptedFindings.title: No event rate or descriptive statistics for variables
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without knowing the outcome proportion and distribution of age, severity, and albumin, readers cannot assess validity of the logistic regression (rare events? linearity assumptions?) nor interpret the odds ratios meaningfully.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Add a table of descriptive statistics: number of events/non-events, mean/SD or median/IQR for continuous covariates, and proportions for categorical ones. Report the event rate explicitly.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Expected table with N, events, and covariate summaries in revised manuscript or a summary-statistics artifact.

acceptedFindings.title: Model fit assessment limited to AIC/BIC; no discrimination or calibration reported
evidenceRefs: stats-run.json: diagnostics contain only AIC, BIC, df_resid
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: AIC/BIC alone do not tell us how well the model discriminates or whether predictions are well calibrated. For an associative study, AUC and Hosmer–Lemeshow are standard.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Compute and report the c-statistic (AUC) and Hosmer–Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test (or a calibration plot). Add these to the diagnostics output.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Presence of 'c_statistic' or 'auc' and 'hosmer_lemeshow' in updated diagnostics.json or figures.

acceptedFindings.title: Missing data handling not described
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: Methods: 'The complete-case sample size was 240. Missingness, eligibility, and sparse-cell concerns are handled as review items...'
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Complete-case analysis can bias results if missingness is not completely at random. The proportion of missing records and any pattern analysis (e.g., observations with missingness associated with outcome) are omitted.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Report the original sample size, number of exclusions, missingness proportions per variable, and any comparison of complete cases versus excluded cases on key characteristics. State the assumed missing-data mechanism.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Existence of a missing-data table or a detailed description in revised manuscript.

acceptedFindings.title: Insufficient information for independent reproduction
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: Reproducibility section: only a run directory artifact inventory hash.
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without describing the data source, variable definitions, and analysis code, another researcher cannot reproduce or verify the results. The artifact hash alone does not guarantee reproducibility.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide a clear data provenance statement (e.g., dataset name, version, access conditions), the statistical software and package versions used, and the analysis script (or a literate document) as supplementary material. If data cannot be shared, describe why and offer a synthetic example.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Inspection of a shared repository or code archive referenced in the revised manuscript.

acceptedFindings.title: P‑value for intercept unnecessarily reported
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: The p‑value for the intercept in logistic regression has no practical interpretation and may confuse readers. Its inclusion detracts from the clinically relevant quantities.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Remove the row for the intercept p‑value from the results table; report the odds ratio and CI if needed, but do not highlight the p‑value.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: The manuscript lists 'For const, the odds ratio was 0.0178 (95% CI 0.0005 to 0.6672); p=0.0293.'

acceptedFindings.title: No sample size or power analysis
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Without a power calculation or justification of sample size, the reader cannot assess whether the study had adequate precision to detect a clinically meaningful effect of treatment. The null‑finding p‑value (0.154) could be due to an underpowered study.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Provide a post‑hoc power calculation for the observed effect size or explain why formal power analysis is not applicable in this exploratory context.

acceptedFindings.title: Inappropriate residual normality test for logistic regression
evidenceRefs: stats-run.json: residual diagnostics include Shapiro–Wilk p = 5.62e-08
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Logistic regression residuals are not normally distributed; reporting a Shapiro–Wilk p-value misleads readers and may prompt unnecessary model tweaks.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Remove the Shapiro–Wilk test from diagnostic output. Use appropriate residual diagnostics for logistic regression (e.g., standardized deviance residuals, calibration plots).
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: stats-run.json still contains 'shapiro_p_value' key after revision.

acceptedFindings.title: Variable coding and units not defined
evidenceRefs: manuscript.md: Variables section: 'Covariates: age, severity, albumin.'
acceptedFindings.whyItMatters: Odds ratios are per unit change, but without units (e.g., years for age, point scales for severity, g/dL for albumin) the magnitude cannot be interpreted.
acceptedFindings.actionableFix: Explicitly state whether each covariate is continuous or categorical, and define the units. If severity is an ordinal scale, describe it.
acceptedFindings.deterministicVerification: Variable definitions table in method section.
